slides.title: Why your wheels wear out too soon
slides.sub: Ten minutes a week keeps a set round and fast

slides.title: Uneven wear is the real culprit
slides.body: You push out and lean into corners, so the inner edge grinds lower. A coned wheel has less contact with the ground and loses grip when you need it most.

slides.title: Move every wheel and flip it
slides.caption: Each wheel moves to a new position and turns over, so the whole set wears evenly.

slides.title: Rotate every one to three sessions
slides.body: Rotate more often on rough outdoor tarmac. After each session, run a fingertip across each wheel. If you feel a clear slope, move it and flip it.

slides.title: Three wheel and Hi Lo frames
slides.body: On three wheels, loop middle to front, front to rear, rear to middle. On a Hi Lo frame, keep the smaller wheel in place and just flip it.

slides.title: Check bearings while wheels are off
slides.body: Wipe grit off the shields, spin each bearing and listen for grinding. Add a drop of skate oil if any sound dry.

slides.text: The exact pattern matters less than doing it consistently.
